The buggy method is `org.apache.commons.lang.StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)`.

Why:
- The failing test expects `StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase("ß", "SS")` to be `false`.
- Its implementation is:

```java
public static boolean containsIgnoreCase(String str, String searchStr) {
    if (str == null || searchStr == null) {
        return false;
    }
    return contains(str.toUpperCase(), searchStr.toUpperCase());
}
```

Root cause:
- `String.toUpperCase()` is not a safe way to implement locale-independent case-insensitive containment.
- Some Unicode characters expand during case conversion, notably German sharp s: `"ß".toUpperCase()` can become `"SS"`.
- So this method transforms:
  - `str = "ß"` into `"SS"`
  - `searchStr = "SS"` into `"SS"`
- Then `contains("SS", "SS")` returns `true`, producing the false positive seen in the test.

This also violates the intended locale independence because `toUpperCase()` without an explicit locale depends on the default JVM locale.

The dynamic verification came back inconclusive only because it did not reach the failing invocation, but the static evidence directly matches the observed failure.

The buggy method is `org.apache.commons.lang.StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)`.

Why:
- The failing test expects `StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase("ß", "SS")` to be `false`.
- Its implementation is:

```java
public static boolean containsIgnoreCase(String str, String searchStr) {
    if (str == null || searchStr == null) {
        return false;
    }
    return contains(str.toUpperCase(), searchStr.toUpperCase());
}
```

Root cause:
- `String.toUpperCase()` is not a safe way to implement locale-independent case-insensitive containment.
- Some Unicode characters expand during case conversion, notably German sharp s: `"ß".toUpperCase()` can become `"SS"`.
- So this method transforms:
  - `str = "ß"` into `"SS"`
  - `searchStr = "SS"` into `"SS"`
- Then `contains("SS", "SS")` returns `true`, producing the false positive seen in the test.

This also violates the intended locale independence because `toUpperCase()` without an explicit locale depends on the default JVM locale.

The dynamic verification came back inconclusive only because it did not reach the failing invocation, but the static evidence directly matches the observed failure.
